::: {.assignment-intro}
This report investigates whether water quality in the Yarra River changed between the early 1990s and the 2020s. It begins with a detailed audit of site coverage and parameter availability, then focuses on pH, electrical conductivity at 25°C, and nitrogen as indicators that can support a meaningful comparison across the two periods.

## Key findings

- Many candidate measures could not support a historical comparison because they were observed in only one period or had too few records.
- The estimated mean nitrogen level fell from 1.12 in the 1990s to 1.05 in the 2020s, with overlapping confidence intervals.
- Taken together, the pH, conductivity, and nitrogen evidence suggests an overall improvement in water quality, while the report keeps the limitations of uneven monitoring data visible.

The project also uses visual inference to evaluate whether apparent differences could plausibly arise after permuting the period labels.
